azure_blob_archive.accountType: General Purpose v2 / Blob Storage, flat namespace, block blob

notes: Identical to Germany West Central except Archive read operations: 6.0 USD / 5.152 EUR per 10K in West Europe against 5.375 USD / 4.6153 EUR in Germany West Central. Egress tiers are the same (both regions are in Zone 1, 'North America and Europe').

The Azure pricing page renders every rate as '$-' and fills it in client-side, so figures come from Microsoft's Retail Prices API. Meters under productName 'General Block Blob v2' and 'Blob Storage', skuName 'Archive LRS', armRegionName 'germanywestcentral', USD / EUR: 'Archive LRS Data Stored' 0.0018 / 0.0015 per 1 GB/Month; 'Archive LRS Write Operations' 0.12 / 0.103 per 10K; 'Archive Read Operations' 5.375 / 4.6153 per 10K; 'Archive Priority Read Operations' 65.0 / 55.8132 per 10K; 'Archive Data Retrieval' 0.024 / 0.0206 per 1 GB; 'Archive Priority Data Retrieval' 0.13 / 0.1116 per 1 GB; 'Archive LRS Early Delete' 0.0018 / 0.0015 per 1 GB; 'Archive Data Write' 0.0 per 1 GB.
putPer1000 is the listed per-10K write-operation price divided by 10; Azure publishes only the per-10K figure.
EUR figures are the euro prices Microsoft itself publishes in the Retail Prices API (currencyCode=EUR), not a conversion done here. The storage figure is rounded by Microsoft to 4 decimals (0.0015).

Standard vs high priority: 'Archive Data Retrieval' is standard-priority rehydration and 'Archive Priority Data Retrieval' is high priority. A rehydration also incurs the read-operation meter per 10K blobs. There is no bulk tier cheaper than standard.

180-day early deletion, verbatim from the pricing page: 'Any blob that is moved to the Archive tier is subject to an Archive early deletion period of 180 days.' Charged pro rata via the 'Archive LRS Early Delete' meter.

Egress is the Bandwidth service, default Microsoft Global Network routing ('Rtn Preference: MGN'), tier starts (GB): 0 free, 100 at 0.087, 10335 at 0.083, 51295 at 0.07, 153695 at 0.05, 512095 at 0.05. The bandwidth pricing page shows the same numbers for 'From North America, Europe to any destination' and states: 'Azure already offers the first 100 GB/month of egressed data for free to all customers in all Azure regions around the world'. Tier boundaries on that page use 'Note: 1 TB = 1,000 GB'.
No per-blob overhead or minimum billable object size for the Archive tier is stated on the Blob pricing page (no metadata or object-size charge appears there), so both are null.
Hierarchical-namespace (ADLS Gen2) accounts cost more per operation in this region: write 0.156 per 10K, read 6.9875 per 10K, priority read 84.5 per 10K; storage and retrieval rates are the same.
Blob index tags, if used: 'Index Tags' 0.039 USD / 0.0335 EUR per 10K per month.

All Google figures are per gibibyte (GiB). Storage is read from the pricing page's own 'Data storage' region table (single region): 'Frankfurt (europe-west3)' row shows Standard $0.023, Nearline $0.013, Coldline $0.006, Archive '$0.0025 / 1 gibibyte month'; hourly view Archive $0.000003425 / 1 gibibyte hour.

Cross-checked in Google's SKU catalog (cloud.google.com/skus, service 95FF-2EF5-5EA1 Cloud Storage): 'Archive Storage Frankfurt' D9F7-D25F-B0EF, europe-west3, 0.0025 USD / 0.0021455 EUR per 1 gibibyte month; 'Archive Storage Frankfurt (Early Delete)' 0F22-5F50-0592, 0.00008333 USD / 0.000071514 EUR per gibibyte day. Google: 'If you pay in a currency other than USD, the prices listed in your currency on Cloud Platform SKUs apply.'

Operations (pricing page, 'For buckets located in a single region', Archive storage): Class A flat namespace $0.05 per 1,000, hierarchical $0.065; Class B flat $0.05, hierarchical $0.065. SKU catalog agrees: 'Regional Archive Class A Operations' F3A8-B939-4A19 0.05 USD / 0.04291 EUR per 1,000; 'Regional Archive Class B Operations' 1DBA-E3C9-B2A8 0.05 USD per 1,000. Uploads are Class A.

Retrieval (pricing page): Archive storage '$0.05 / 1 gibibyte'. SKU 'Archive Data Retrieval' 27A1-EBA4-49E8, global, 0.05 USD / 0.04291 EUR per gibibyte. Google has one Archive retrieval rate with millisecond access; there is no bulk or priority tier, so retrievalPerGB is a single number.

Egress conflict between two Google sources. The Cloud Storage pricing page, 'General network usage', 'Data transfer to Worldwide Destinations (excluding Asia & Australia)': 0 GiB to 10 TiB $0.12, 10 TiB to 150 TiB $0.11, 150 TiB and above $0.08 per GiB (this table is not region-specific). The SKU catalog's Cloud Storage SKU 22EB-AAE8-FBCD 'Download Worldwide Destinations (excluding Asia & Australia)', global, is tiered differently: 0 to 100 GiB free, 100 GiB to 1 TiB $0.12, 1 TiB to 10 TiB $0.11, 10 TiB and above $0.08 per month per account. The first paid rate ($0.12) agrees; tier boundaries do not. egressTiersPerGiB follows the pricing page.

freeEgressGBPerMonth is null because the sources disagree for a Frankfurt bucket: the pricing page says 'Cloud Storage Always Free quotas apply to usage in US-WEST1, US-CENTRAL1, and US-EAST1 regions' and lists the data-transfer allowance as '100 GB from North America to each Google Cloud Data transfer destination (Australia and China excluded)', while the global download SKU shows its first 100 GiB per month per account at $0.00. A conservative model uses 0; at most it is 100 GiB a month.
Minimum storage duration table: Standard None, Nearline 30 days, Coldline 90 days, Archive 365 days. Deleting early is charged as if stored for the minimum duration.
No per-object overhead or minimum billable object size is published for Archive on the pricing page, so both are null.

notes.text: Method: vendor sources only. AWS figures come from the price maps that aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing loads (data-pricing-endpoint b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps) and were cross-checked against the AWS Price List Bulk API files for eu-central-1; every figure matched. Azure figures come from Microsoft's Retail Prices API (USD and EUR), with policy text from the Azure pricing pages. Google figures come from the tables embedded in cloud.google.com/storage/pricing, cross-checked in Google's SKU catalog. Backblaze and Wasabi figures come from their own pricing pages, FAQs and docs. No third-party source was used.

Frankfurt costs more than other EU regions at all three hyperscalers. AWS Deep Archive is $0.0018/GB-month in EU (Frankfurt), EU (London), EU (Paris), EU (Milan) and EU (Spain) but $0.00099 in EU (Ireland) and EU (Stockholm), the same as us-east-1 (Zurich $0.00198). Flexible Retrieval is $0.00405 in Frankfurt against $0.0036 in Ireland and Stockholm. Deep Archive bulk retrieval is $0.005/GB in Frankfurt against $0.003 in Ireland and Stockholm.

Azure Archive LRS storage by European region (USD/GB-month, General Block Blob v2): North Europe, Sweden Central, Sweden South 0.00099; Norway East 0.001416; Germany West Central, Germany North, West Europe, France Central, Italy North, Spain Central, UK South 0.0018; Norway West 0.00184; Switzerland North 0.00198; UK West 0.0025; France South 0.00304; Switzerland West 0.00351.

Google Archive single-region storage in Europe (USD per GiB-month, pricing page): Belgium (europe-west1), Netherlands (europe-west4) and Finland (europe-north1) $0.0012; Madrid $0.0021; Frankfurt, Berlin, London, Paris, Milan, Turin, Warsaw, Zurich, Stockholm $0.0025.

Units: AWS and Azure both bill storage in binary gigabytes, the same unit Google calls a gibibyte. AWS: 'Amazon S3 storage usage is calculated in binary gigabytes (GB), where 1 GB is 2^30 bytes. This unit of measurement is also known as a gibibyte (GiB)'. Azure: 'Azure Blob Storage usage is calculated in binary Gigabytes (GB), where 1 GB = 2^30 bytes.' Wasabi also uses 1 TB = 1024 GB. So the '7% GiB penalty' applied to Google alone (US data file note; build_articles.py line 283) is not a Google-only effect. Tape capacities are decimal, so pricing a decimal TB as 1000 x the per-GB rate overstates AWS, Azure, Google and Wasabi storage by about 7.4% (1 TB = 931.3 GiB). Azure's bandwidth page uses 'Note: 1 TB = 1,000 GB' for egress tier boundaries.

Taxes: the AWS pricing page says 'our prices are exclusive of applicable taxes and duties, including VAT', and Wasabi's FAQ says its price 'does not include applicable taxes'. No VAT statement was found on the Azure, Google or Backblaze pages fetched.

Currencies: AWS, Backblaze and Wasabi publish these prices in USD only. Microsoft publishes its own EUR prices in the Retail Prices API, and Google publishes EUR prices in its SKU catalog; both are recorded in the *EUR fields. Everything else is USD as listed.

Price changes: no 2025 or 2026 change for Google Cloud Storage appears on its pricing-announce page (it lists only the October 1, 2022 and April 1, 2023 updates). Wasabi's $7.99/TB move on July 1, 2026 covers EMEA and is already in force. The AWS maps were published 2026-09-11 (Deep Archive), 2026-09-16 (data transfer) and 2026-09-18 (S3).
